::: {.cite-bar .domain-intelligence}
[Partly expired]{.status .status-partly-expired} [Pub. L. 114-23]{.cite} [129 Stat. 268]{.cite}
:::

The legislative response to the 2013 Snowden disclosures. It ended bulk collection of domestic telephone records and required that records requests be tied to a specific selection term.

## Key provisions

- Banned bulk collection under Section 215, pen register authority, and national security letters.
- Replaced the bulk telephone metadata program with targeted requests to carriers.
- Created a panel of outside experts who can argue before the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court in novel cases.
- Required declassification review of significant court opinions and added transparency reporting.

## Why it matters

It was the first statute since [FISA](fisa-1978.qmd) to cut back surveillance authority. It amended both that act and the [USA PATRIOT Act](patriot-2001.qmd). The replacement call records program was shut down by the National Security Agency in 2019.

## Current status

Its structural reforms are in force. The authorities it extended (business records, roving wiretaps, lone wolf) expired on March 15, 2020.
